title: Final, sealed, non-sealed or open

blocks.text: Every permitted subtype of a sealed type must say how the hierarchy goes on, with exactly one of three modifiers:

items: `sealed`: only the subtypes it permits may extend it;

blocks.text: A class with no sealed supertype needs none of them and is simply open.
Write `static String kindOf(Class<?> type)` that reads these rules off a loaded class with reflection and returns one of `"final"`, `"sealed"`, `"non-sealed"` or `"open"`:

items: `"final"` when the type is final (a record is implicitly final);
`"sealed"` when the type is sealed (`Class.isSealed()`), a class or an interface;
`"non-sealed"` when it is neither, and one of its **direct** supertypes (its superclass or an interface it names directly) is sealed;

blocks.text: **Examples** (with `sealed interface Pet permits Cat, Dog, Fish`)

cases.says: A final class, a sealed class or interface, a non-sealed subclass and a plain class are each named for what they are.
A class that implements a sealed interface and is neither final nor sealed is non-sealed.
A class extending a non-sealed class is open again: only a sealed direct supertype makes a class non-sealed.

concepts: A permitted subtype must be final, sealed or non-sealed, and non-sealed only applies directly under a sealed supertype.
